{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZfWfXA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDGhFg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 39, "title": "Schedule and retain VDP2 rotation image fetches", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `5e44b280178499f3abd5b69b233b3a3a1efa6c3a`, normal backgrounds acquire image operands through scheduled display events, but rotation backgrounds still fetch missing words during rendering:

- `src/vdp2/fetch.rs:61–70` explicitly bypasses scheduled acquisition for RBG0 and rotation access through the NBG0/RBG1 path.
- `display_active` at lines 129–130 considers only normal-background enable bits. The acquisition loop handles normal layers and skips dual-rotation display.
- `display_word` at lines 285–299 samples backing VRAM on a serializer miss during scanout.

Consequently, rotation image acquisition has no independent hardware-time progression or retained address/data stream comparable to normal backgrounds. Existing static rotation pixels and CPU bank-exclusion tests do not establish when rotation image words were acquired. This matters to raster changes, buffered writes around blanking, shared-bank ownership and deterministic rendering.

## Expected outcome

Acquire RBG0 tile/bitmap and RBG1 tile image operands through deterministic display deadlines. Retain acquired names, character/bitmap words and their address interpretation until consumption. Production scanout must consume those operands without filling image misses from current VRAM.

Primary contract:

- [VDP2 User’s Manual §3.3, display-period VRAM access](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p03_30.htm): rotation accesses occupy dedicated banks independently of normal cycle commands; RBG1 fixes names to B1 and characters to B0.
- [§6.2, rotation display control and RAMCTL](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p06_20.htm): bank assignments, image separation and address eligibility.
- ST-058-R2 §§4.4–4.8 and §6.1 for image layouts and rotation address generation; §6.3 for parameter-read/reload behavior.

Write a primary-derived transaction contract before using implementation output as an oracle. Specify access geometry, ordering, retention, bank ownership and supported display-mode restrictions. Clearly distinguish documented requirements from deterministic phase assumptions; #19’s two-cycle normal-screen lead is not evidence of rotation latency. Reconcile applicable manual corrections autonomously with exact references.

## Context and reproduction

Read-only inspection confirms the bypass above. No implementation changes or full acceptance-suite reruns were performed during planning.

Build on `Raster::display_slot`, `Bus::acquire_display`, existing transaction arbitration and normal acquisition infrastructure. Keep the change focused on rotation **image** acquisition. Preserve coefficient interpretation, composition and RPRCTL behavior, retaining the inputs necessary to prevent later changes from reinterpreting already acquired image operands. Separate coefficient-table acquisition timing, general video-register readback and unrelated rasterizer corrections remain outside this increment.

Issue #19 explicitly deferred rotation acquisition. Issue #35 implemented one-shot parameter reload requests; its evidence must remain valid. Do not consume requests early or twice through address preview, replay or debugger inspection. Any necessary correction to an inherited technical assumption must retain meaningful coverage and cite affirmative primary evidence.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document the rotation image transaction contract with exact manual sections and applicable corrections. Identify unresolved physical phases as assumptions, without claiming measured hardware latency.
- [ ] Schedule image acquisition when only rotation screens are enabled. Implement RBG0 tile/bitmap and RBG1 tile paths, including supported name widths, character sizes and color formats. Respect dedicated-bank roles, split/unsplit geometry and RBG1’s fixed B0/B1 routing; normal cycle words must not control rotation-owned banks.
- [ ] Retain acquired words and address metadata across later memory/register changes. Repeated addresses must acquire again when the contract requires a new transfer. Scanout cannot repair missing image operands through live VRAM reads. Preserve non-mutating debugger previews.
- [ ] Add independently authored native vectors with literal addresses, words and pixels. Cover nonsequential rotated sampling, repeated-address revisits, tile boundaries, both name widths, every supported image color format, bitmap data, RBG1, bank eligibility and rotation alongside normal backgrounds where permitted. Expectations must not call production address/timing helpers.
- [ ] Add boundary tests for writes before, at and after acquisition, retained data before consumption, CPU/DMA waits and independent-bank progress. Exercise both SH-2 adapters, representative on-chip DMAC and SCU DMA routes, final-write/IRQ ordering, blanking release, reset cancellation and absence of stale operands. Results and traces must agree across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and debugger inspection.
- [ ] Add an original MIT-licensed guest diagnostic with reproducible source, builder, hashes and authored expectations. Guest instructions must configure RBG0/RBG1, initialize images and perform legal timed image or bank-control changes that distinguish acquisition from later scanout. Include changed-source, changed-timing and omitted-write controls, guest-computed records and repeated cold boots. Host code may load media and inspect results, but must not supply device setup or rendered output.
- [ ] Execute identical guest bytes in native Machine tests and rebuilt production browser Wasm under `/saturn-rust/`. Assert independent framebuffer pixels and actual Canvas pixels. Demonstrate an executed negative control in which the inherited render-time image-fetch path fails the distinguishing assertions.
- [ ] Preserve existing normal-fetch, rotation reload, sprite rotation, coefficient/window/composition and bus regressions. Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab must retain their existing gameplay, restart, graphics, audio and diagnostic checks. Correct mistaken expectations only with documented primary evidence and equivalent or stronger coverage.
- [ ] Update architecture, the conformance matrix and a focused validation record with implementation/test links, actual commands/results, phase assumptions and remaining deviations. Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native/Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, all registered fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh` and the complete extended `npm run test:browser` without required skips.

This is partial #17 work. Coefficient/other table acquisition timing, remaining CPU/peripheral and board/reset behavior, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration acceptance remain mandatory. Do not reopen historical trackers or infer umbrella completion from this merge, Issue state or green CI. Genuine BIOS and commercial-game compatibility remain not independently confirmed.

## Optional validation

Additional original rotation stress scenes are useful. Personal firmware, commercial media, physical hardware, human approval and live Pages inspection are not required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
